- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model underestimates upside — add 2–4% buffer to forecast mean.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a rally, model fails to reverse — apply mean reversion to forecast, targeting 1–2% below recent 7-day high.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 2–5 days — shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day for each lagged day.
- When multiple auction events occur in 7-day window, model overestimates supply impact — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
